findings.file: data/units/ra2.json (ra2.soviet.siege-chopper: roles.secondary, armament/1/damage, uncertain/1, as_player, memorable)
findings.summary: Commit a3c4d6d changed the Siege Chopper's howitzer from lobbed artillery to a direct-fire cannon. It did not change the two values that rested on the artillery coding. roles.secondary still lists siege, and armament/1/damage is still explosive, the artillery family's default. The checker's verdicts on both fields come from before this recode.
findings.evidence:
`git show a3c4d6d -- data/units/ra2.json` changes only family artillery->cannon, delivery lobbed->projectile, the atypical entry and the weakness link. roles stays {primary anti-infantry, secondary [siege, anti-air]} and armament/1 stays damage explosive with traits []. The unit's own uncertain/0 says no source shows the howitzer hitting an area. The wiki infobox (cache wiki_Siege_chopper) gives the gun only '90 (deployed) (SCHOPWH)', range 12, with no area. The profile (cache newsovietinfo2.jsp, id_ form) gives 'Application line: an anti-infantry gun that also serves as ground artillery.

Rules: fields.md roles.secondary says a role's coding rule applies there just as for the primary, unless the rule says As primary. Siege's coding rule (vocabularies.md, roles) accepts only a lobbed weapon reaching long or further, dropped bombs, a deploy-mode gun reaching long or further that hits an area, or a long-range missile or rocket built mainly to destroy structures. It also says a long-range missile or cannon alone is not siege. So the Application line's 'artillery' cannot give siege without area damage.

fields.md armament[].damage step 5: with no damage map, use the family default unless the weapon is built mainly to bring down aircraft or its hit is a blast that hurts an area. The cannon family's default is armour-piercing.

The unit's uncertain/1 already says that without the other role, raider (very fast with light armour) would take the second slot. Its as_player still says the howitzer 'lobs shells', and memorable says it 'flies the artillery'.
findings.fix:
In ra2.soviet.siege-chopper:
- Set armament/1/damage to "armour-piercing".
- Set roles.secondary to ["anti-air", "raider"]: anti-air ranks at step 3 (its machine gun) and raider at step 4 (very fast, light armour).
- Rewrite uncertain/1 to say siege is left out because a direct-fire cannon with no area hit fails siege's coding rule, which applies to roles.secondary, even though the Application line says artillery.
- In as_player, change 'lobs shells at buildings' to 'fires shells at buildings'. In memorable, change 'it flies the artillery wherever it is wanted' to 'it flies a heavy gun wherever it is wanted'.

If a cited source is found showing the deployed shell hurting an area instead, add the splash trait, keep explosive and siege, and cite that source.

verdict.reason: Commit a3c4d6d recoded the howitzer as a direct-fire cannon but left two values that depended on the old artillery coding. Siege's coding rule applies to roles.secondary (fields.md: 'A role's coding rule binds here as for the primary'). It accepts a deploy-mode gun only if the gun hits an area, and it says a long-range cannon alone is not siege. No source shows an area hit. Step 1 of roles.secondary only ranks roles that already qualify, so the Application line's word 'artillery' cannot bring siege back. Damage step 5 gives the cannon default, armour-piercing. The batch already did exactly this for the Slave Miner's elite cannon firing high-explosive rounds but has no sourced area hit. The checker passed both fields before the recode.
verdict.evidence: `git show a3c4d6d -- data/units/ra2.json` changes only armament/1's family (artillery to cannon), its delivery (lobbed to projectile), the atypical entry and the weakness link. roles stays {anti-infantry, [siege, anti-air]}, and armament/1 keeps damage explosive with traits []. docs/vocabularies.md gives siege's coding rule. docs/fields.md line 42 has the roles.secondary rule. On the unit, uncertain armament/1/traits says no source shows a shell hurting an area, and uncertain/1 says 'Siege comes from step 1 (the Application line says artillery)' and that raider (very fast, light armour) would otherwise take the slot. Opening coder A already noted that a cannon would need an area hit for siege (research/r1/opening/hesitations.md line 95). research/registry-notes/games-r1.md line 178 says RA2 has no damage map, so step 5 applies, and the cannon default is armour-piercing. The Slave Miner's uncertain armament/1/damage applies the same rule. as_player still says 'lobs shells'. The checker commit e54f737 (2026-10-22 21:25) predates a3c4d6d (2026-10-23 01:59). No cached rules data gives the shell an area.
verdict.better_fix: Apply the proposed fix, with these additions. (1) Before ranking anti-air at step 3, check roles.secondary step 2, the cannon the deploy mode switches to. No game data, official text or source gives it a bonus against armour or calls it strong against vehicles, so it adds no role and [anti-air, raider] stands. (2) In uncertain/1, say that the Application line still names artillery, but siege is not a candidate because its coding rule fails. (3) In games-r1.md, RA2 Official role lines, add to 'anti-infantry and artillery, so siege (Siege Chopper)' that siege must still pass its coding rule, and with the gun now a cannon it does not. (4) In README Decisions item 8, add that the Siege Chopper loses siege. Re-run the copy-check on the reworded text and npm run check:merge.

findings.summary: Three RA2 entries stay at confidence high although each has an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree on a point that decides a coded term. The confidence tie-break drops such an entry to medium, as the batch itself did for the Field Mechanic and the Mobile Gap Generator.
findings.evidence:
Rule (data/vocab/confidence.json, tie-break high/medium): when sites or pages of one site contradict each other and no official text settles it, record sources_disagree. Then drop to medium only when a contradicted point decides a term the entry codes, such as a weapon's family or damage, a band, a role or the tier.

(1) Slave Miner, uncertain/9, path armament/1/family, sources_disagree true. The Slave miner page's infobox says 'Cannon when elite' and its prose 'tank gun'. The War miner page's prose (cache wiki_War_miner) says the gun becomes a strong autocannon when upgraded. The coded family is cannon. No official text covers the elite gun. Confidence is high.

(2) Mastermind, uncertain/5, path mobility/base, sources_disagree true: the voxel render shows tracks, while a Yuri (faction) caption says wheels. Also uncertain/3, path sensors/traits, sources_disagree true, against YR manual Gameplay Changes item 20. Confidence is high.

(3) Boris (sampled, but confidence is not among his checked paths in checks.json), uncertain/0, path armour/models, sources_disagree true: the YR manual says heroes regenerate, while the infobox gives healing only at Elite. Confidence is high.

Precedent: rule-problems.md item 10 follow-up (a3c4d6d) set the Field Mechanic to medium because 'his armour type decides his armour class and no official text settles it'. The Mobile Gap Generator is medium for its speed clash.
findings.fix: Set confidence to "medium" on ra2.yuri.slave-miner, ra2.yuri.mastermind and ra2.soviet.boris. If the Mastermind's 'on wheels' caption is judged a figure of speech rather than a contradiction, remove sources_disagree from its uncertain/5. Its uncertain/3 (sensors/traits, which the registry requires to be flagged) still keeps it at medium.

verdict.reason: Each of the three units has a sources_disagree entry on a point that decides a coded term, and no official text settles it. For Boris and the Mastermind, the registry itself sets the official line aside and orders the flag. The confidence tie-break then drops the unit to medium, which is what the batch did for the Field Mechanic (armour class) and the Mobile Gap Generator (speed). Boris is the clearest case: the flag decides armour.models. The Mastermind's 'on wheels' flag is a figure of speech, but its flag on sensors/traits (ordered by the registry) decides the detector trait. The Slave Miner's case is the weakest of the three, because the family tie-break goes by rate of fire, not name. Still, the War miner page's 'auto-cannon' implies rapid fire against the infobox's slow rate, and the coder flagged the clash at the family path and listed autocannon as the alternative.
verdict.evidence: The confidence tie-break is in docs/vocabularies.md line 436. In data/units/ra2.json all three read confidence high. Boris: uncertain/0 at armour/models, marked sources_disagree (the YR manual says heroes regenerate; the infobox lists healing only at Elite). games-r1.md line 381 orders: follow the infobox, no self-repair model, flag sources_disagree. Mastermind: uncertain/3 at sensors/traits, as games-r1.md line 386 orders (Gameplay Changes item 20, but no page confirms the Mastermind). Mastermind uncertain/5 at mobility/base: the Yuri (faction) caption's 'on wheels', which the note itself calls 'apparently a figure of speech'. Slave Miner: uncertain/9 at armament/1/family, cannon against the War miner page's auto-cannon. The j08 hesitation lists autocannon as the alternative, and no official text covers the elite gun. rule-problems.md item 10 follow-up: the Field Mechanic falls to medium because his armour type decides his armour class.
verdict.better_fix: Apply the proposed fix: medium on all three, and remove sources_disagree from the Mastermind's uncertain/5 while keeping its note. Run the same test on the other high units that carry sources_disagree. ra2.allied.chrono-legionnaire uncertain/0 at mobility/speed is the same case: the wiki says land speed sets how fast he re-emerges, ModEnc says only distance counts, and the band is a judgement. It decides the speed band but stayed high (fill hesitations line 291), so it needs the same decision. The other flags decide no term: the Mammoth's and Yak's armour notes and Tanya's tier/gate say 'either way', and the Chaos Drone's tier and cost and Boris's cost_band are older figures that the manual's tech table and the infobox settle. If Mustafa reads flags the registry orders as already settled, write that into the tie-break instead.

findings.file: data/units/ra1.json, ra2.json, ra3.json (review of the 9 sampled units)
findings.summary: The nine units the checker sampled and checked field by field still have review.status 'unchecked', with no checked_by, checked_on, checked_paths or wrong_paths. The data therefore contradicts the checker record.
findings.evidence:
fields.md defines review as 'Checker status. The research run samples entries and re-checks them against their sources.' Its status is one of unchecked, checked or disputed, with checked_by, checked_on, checked_paths and wrong_paths.

research/r1/checker/checks.json lists the fields checked on ra1.allied.minelayer, ra1.allied.mobile-gap-generator, ra1.soviet.yak, ra2.iraq.desolator, ra2.soviet.boris, ra2.soviet.siege-chopper, ra3.allied.tanya, ra3.empire.mecha-tengu and ra3.empire.sudden-transport (370 fields per the README). result.json lists six fixed unit fields: minelayer on_death.notes, MGG sources[1].supports, Yak uncertain[6], Desolator body.plan and sources/2/supports, Tanya armament[1].can_target.

All nine units read `"review": {"status": "unchecked"}` (dumped with a script). No script or workflow writes this field (`grep review research/workflows/checker.js` finds nothing).
findings.fix: On each of the nine sampled units, set review to {"status": "checked", "checked_by": "batch r1 checker (research/workflows/checker.js)", "checked_on": "2026-10-22", "checked_paths": [the unit's paths from research/r1/checker/checks.json], "wrong_paths": [its confirmed paths from result.json, e.g. on_death/notes for ra1.allied.minelayer], "notes": "fixed in b46b01c / 0c3d4e2 / dcc4080"}. Use an empty wrong_paths list for Boris, the Siege Chopper, the Mecha Tengu and the Sudden Transport.

verdict.reason: The schema defines review as the checker status, and the checker checked these nine units field by field. They still read unchecked, so the data contradicts the checker record. No step in the runbook or the workflows writes the field. The generated docs therefore print 'review: unchecked' for units that were checked. This is a minor record problem plus a gap in the procedure.
verdict.evidence: A script shows all 28 units and all 36 pattern files read {"status": "unchecked"}. research/r1/checker/checks.json lists the checked paths for the nine sampled units. result.json lists the wrong fields, fixed in 0c3d4e2, b46b01c and dcc4080, and 33 checked pattern files. schemas/common.schema.json defines review with status, checked_by, checked_on, checked_paths, wrong_paths and notes. The workflows code-units.js, reconcile.js and patterns.js only set the field to unchecked, and docs/research-runbook.md never mentions writing it. scripts/build-docs.mjs lines 789 and 840 print '(review: <status>)'. The pilot's sample units on origin/main were never set either, so nothing yet does this.
verdict.better_fix: Apply the proposed fix, with these additions. (1) Also set review on the 33 pattern files the checker covered, which carry the same review group. (2) Write checked_paths in fields.md's slash form; checks.json mixes tier.band, armament/0/family and abilities[0].kind. (3) Leave out, or name in review.notes, the paths a3c4d6d changed after the check: both Minelayers' mobility/traits (crush added) and the Siege Chopper's armament/1 family and delivery, plus its roles and damage if F1 is fixed. (4) Use status checked, not disputed, since the confirmed errors were fixed, with checked_on 2026-10-22. (5) Add a step to the runbook's checker section (and to the checker workflow) that writes review on every sampled unit and pattern, so R2 does it from the start.

findings.summary: The Magnetron and the Slave Miner each cite three Command & Conquer Wiki pages and no other non-official site, although CNCNZ's Yuri's units page covers both units. The batch read that page, and the Chaos Drone cites it. The Magnetron's third wiki page is the manual transcript, which repeats the manual PDF it already cites.
findings.evidence:
Rule (fields.md sources[]): when another established site covers the unit, cite it rather than a third page of the same site.

Magnetron sources: the profile, cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Magnetron, /wiki/Magnetic_beam, the YR manual PDF, and /wiki/Command_%26_Conquer:_Red_Alert_2_-_Yuri%27s_Revenge_manual (the transcript). The transcript's supports (roles, body, weaknesses/0, countered_by/0, combos/0) are already backed by sources/3, the PDF.

Slave Miner sources: the profile, /wiki/Slave_miner, /wiki/Slave_(Yuri%27s_Revenge), the YR PDF, and /wiki/War_miner.

CNCNZ page https://cncnz.com/games/yuris-revenge/yuris-units/ (cache cncnz.com/games_yuris-revenge_yuris-units, fetched 2026-10-20) has its own Magnetron entry (cost, Psychic Radar, lifts vehicles, damages structures, no way to crush infantry). It also has Slave Miner and Slave entries: deploys and releases Slaves, free replacement, Slaves join their 'liberators'. games-r1.md calls CNCNZ 'a long-running fan site', kind guide. ra2.yuri.chaos-drone already cites this page.

Magnetron: replace sources/4 (the transcript) with {url: https://cncnz.com/games/yuris-revenge/yuris-units/, title: 'Red Alert 2 - Yuri's Revenge: Yuri's Units, CNCNZ.com', kind: guide}, supporting armament/0 and weaknesses/0, and move the transcript's supports to sources/3.

verdict.reason: Both units cite three Command & Conquer Wiki pages and no other non-official site, yet CNCNZ's Yuri's units page has its own entry for each. The batch treats a guide-kind fan site as the other established site for this rule (StrategyWiki for RA1, rule-problems item 11). The j08 coder looked for a second site only on StrategyWiki and missed CNCNZ. No code or confidence changes; this is only about following the citation rule. Severity minor. One caveat: the RA2 notes do not yet name CNCNZ for this rule, as the RA1 notes name StrategyWiki, so that reading needs writing down.
verdict.evidence: In ra2.json, the Magnetron cites the official profile, wiki/Magnetron, wiki/Magnetic_beam, the YR manual PDF and the wiki's YR manual transcript. The PDF is not counted as a wiki page (games-r1.md line 206). Every path the transcript supports is already in the PDF's supports. The Slave Miner cites the profile, wiki/Slave_miner, wiki/Slave_(Yuri's_Revenge), the PDF and wiki/War_miner. The CNCNZ page (cache cncnz.com games_yuris-revenge_yuris-units, fetched 2026-10-20) has its own Magnetron entry: $1000, Psychic Radar, lifts vehicles and ships toward itself, damages structures, has no weapon that works against infantry and cannot crush them, poorly armoured. Its Slave Miner entry: $1750, deploys and releases up to five Slaves, repairs itself while mobile, Engineer repair when deployed, free replacements, and Slaves join their liberators. Its Slave entry says they cannot be ordered. The prices match both entries. The Chaos Drone cites this page as sources/4. research/r1/fill/j08-ra2/report.json source_problems item 4 says StrategyWiki has no page for either unit, 'so every source but the manual is from the Command & Conquer Wiki'. games-r1.md line 225 (StrategyWiki is the other site for this rule, though its kind stays guide) is RA1 only, and line 450 makes CNCNZ kind guide. Of the 28 units, only these two have a third page of one site and no second site.
verdict.better_fix: (1) In the RA2 notes, or the R1 Research notes' CNCNZ line, say that CNCNZ is the other established site for the third-page rule, kind still guide, as the RA1 notes say for StrategyWiki. (2) Magnetron: replace sources/4 (the transcript) with CNCNZ, supporting armament/0, weaknesses/0 and countered_by/0. Moving the transcript's supports changes nothing, since sources/3 already lists them all. The Tank Bunker point stays backed by the PDF note (page 23) and by the Tank bunker page named in uncertain body/plan. CNCNZ's 'significant damage to structures' sits uneasily with weaknesses/4 (slow, weak building damage), so do not cite it for that path, or add an uncertain note. (3) Slave Miner: replace sources/2 (the Slave page) with CNCNZ, supporting abilities/0, abilities/1, on_death and strengths/4. The radiation point in weaknesses/2 is already on the cited Slave miner page (sources/1). The only points that rest on the Slave page alone are that freed Slaves cannot mine and that the ore they carried is lost (on_death notes); name the Slave page in the on_death uncertain entry for those. Dropping the War miner page instead also works: it is about another unit, and every code it carries is already named in uncertain entries. Run the copy-check on the new source notes.

findings.summary: The lay-mines snare-trap variant lets a T1 card freeze its victim, which breaks decision 5B (stuns and freezes only from T2). freeze-and-shatter puts the same cold trap at T2.

Its overrides set only adds_strengths and adds_weaknesses, so the base generator.min_tier "t1" (line 508) applies. Decision 5 in docs/proposal.md (lines 311-316) covers 'Hard crowd control (stuns and freezes that stop the victim acting)', and option B, stuns only from T2, was chosen (line 283: '1B 2A 3C 4B 5B ...'). The stun weapon trait has min_tier t2 (data/vocab/weapon-traits.json). In the batch's own freeze-and-shatter, a frozen target 'can't move, fire or use abilities'. Its generator.min_tier is t2, and its cold-trap variant (line 320) cites the same Halo Wars 2 Cryogenic Generator that snare-trap's seen_in cites. Other variants spell out the gate: burrow's erupt says '(a brief stun only from T2 up)' and passenger-sets-weapon's tool-seat says '(a stun only on T2 and higher carriers)'. A script over all variants (summary mentions stun or freeze, effective min_tier below t2) flagged only this one as ungated.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The snare-trap variant has no min_tier override, so it inherits t1, and its text lets a T1 trap freeze its victim. The batch itself treats a full stop as covered by decision 5B: disable-machine's changes_from_rts says a full shutdown is a stun for vehicles, so under 5B it comes only from T2. freeze-and-shatter is t2, and its cold-trap variant inherits t2. My own scan of every batch variant found no other enemy freeze or stun below T2. teleport frozen-arrival and burrow hide-in-place are effects on the user, not on an enemy. One caveat that does not save it: the vocab gates only the stun trait (weapon-traits.json min_tier t2), and rule problem 11 (code a freeze as root plus silence) is still open. findings.summary: Four variants inherit a base adds_weakness that their own text contradicts, because they don't override it. A card rolled with them would carry a false weakness.
findings.evidence: The schema says variants[].overrides.adds_weaknesses 'Replaces the base generator's adds_weaknesses for this variant', so without an override the base text applies. (1) burrow.json variants/6 buried-strike (lines 422-427) has no overrides and says 'One attack works from below without surfacing'. The base adds_weaknesses (line 471) says 'It can't attack from below: it must come up first'. (2) capture-structure.json variants/4 clamp-a-device (lines 300-307) overrides only kinds and says 'you are free to move'. The base (line 373) says 'It has to reach the structure and stay next to it while the work runs, exposed and unable to shoot'. variants/6 hack-from-range ('Works from a short distance, so you can stay behind cover') has no overrides either. (3) lock-in-stasis.json variants/5 return-displacement (lines 327-332) has no overrides and says 'anything standing there when they return is destroyed, and the returning units are badly hurt too'. The base (line 369) says it 'deals no damage ... it returns unharmed'. (4) disguise.json variants/2 prop-when-still (line 274) overrides only kinds and says 'firing makes you flicker for a moment, and moving ends it'. The base (line 334) says 'The cover ends when it attacks or is hit'.
findings.fix: Add overrides.adds_weaknesses to each variant. buried-strike: [{"ref":"mobility-trait:burrow","why":"Only its one buried strike works from below and using it shows where it is; everything else needs it to come up first."}]. clamp-a-device: [{"ref":"pattern:capture-structure","why":"It must get close enough to stick the device on, and enemies can knock the device off."}]. hack-from-range: [{"ref":"pattern:capture-structure","why":"Starting the hack gives its position away, and it must stay in reach until the hack ends."}]. return-displacement: [{"ref":"pattern:lock-in-stasis","why":"Holds one target at a time, and its return hurts the target and wrecks whatever stands in its place, friend or foe."}]. prop-when-still: [{"ref":"pattern:disguise","why":"Moving ends the cover and firing makes it flicker, and once found it is usually fragile."}].

verdict.reason: Confirmed for all five variants. The schema says a variant's adds_weaknesses replaces the base list, so a variant without one inherits the base text. Each base text is contradicted by its variant's own summary. buried-strike strikes from below, but inherits 'can't attack from below'. clamp-a-device leaves you 'free to move' and hack-from-range 'works from a short distance', but both inherit 'stay next to it ... exposed'. return-displacement destroys things and badly hurts the returning units, but inherits 'deals no damage ... returns unharmed'. prop-when-still only flickers when firing and ends when moving, but inherits 'cover ends when it attacks or is hit'. findings.summary: Since commit fcfe9f6, mkws.sh's path guard accepts relative paths, which the earlier guard refused. Neither version ever refused paths with '..' or paths that go on past the ws- folder. So 'rm -rf' can delete a folder outside any workspace, while the runbook says mkws.sh refuses any other kind of path.
findings.evidence: Guard at 60a962f: case "$WS" in /*/ws-*) (absolute paths only). Current guard (fcfe9f6), line 6: case "$WS" in */working folder/r*/*/ws-*). I tested both patterns with a scratch script that only matches and does nothing (guardtest2.sh). './working folder/r1/fill/ws-j01': old refuses, new accepts. 'r2/working folder/r2/fill/ws-j01': old refuses, new accepts. '/s/working folder/r1/fill/ws-j01/../../../../..' and '/s/working folder/r1/fill/ws-j01/../../../../..the home folder/MoesTools-Brainstormer': both accept. '/s/working folder/r1/fill/ws-j01/data': accepted. The next line runs rm -rf "$WS" on whatever was accepted. With a relative path, rm and mkdir act in the caller's folder, but cd "$REPO" comes before the copy, so cp --parents and cp -r .cache write relative to the repository. Run from the repository root, as the runbook asks, that puts the copy inside the repository. Runbook, Safety section: "workspace copies, and only through mkws.sh (it refuses any other kind of path)"; section 3 says the same. Correct use still works: run on <working folder>/r1/progress/final-review/review-tooling/ws-sample, it made 220 files, the .cache folder and the node_modules link, and it refused a temporary folder and a path that does not end in ws-<job> with exit 2. No test covers mkws.sh.
findings.fix:
Replace line 6 of mkws.sh with:
WS="${1%/}"
usage() { echo "usage: mkws.sh <working folder>/r<N>/<phase>/ws-<job> (an absolute path)" >&2; exit 2; }
case "$WS" in /*) ;; *) usage;; esac
case "$WS/" in */../*|*/./*) usage;; esac
case "$WS" in */working folder/r[0-9]*/*/ws-*) ;; *) usage;; esac
case "${WS##*/}" in ws-?*) ;; *) usage;; esac
Then add a test, skipped on Windows, that runs mkws.sh on a relative path, on <tmp>/working folder/r1/x/ws-a/.. and on <tmp>/working folder/r1/x/ws-a/data. Each must exit 2 and leave the folders untouched.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The fcfe9f6 guard accepts some relative paths that the 60a962f guard refused. Neither guard refuses '..' segments or a path that goes on past the ws- folder. So the runbook's claim (section 3 and Safety) that mkws.sh refuses any other kind of path is false. Damage needs a malformed argument, for example a '..' path that resolves to a phase folder holding other jobs' workspaces and notes, or to the repository itself. Still, this guard is the only safety on an rm -rf that the night shift runs with nobody watching. The proposed guard is right.
verdict.evidence: Compared git show 60a962f:research/workflows/mkws.sh (case /*/ws-*) with the current l.6 (case */working folder/r*/*/ws-*), using a match-only sh script under dash. A path starting with ./ and one starting with r2/ are refused by the old guard and accepted by the new one. '<...>/ws-j01/../../../../..', '<...>/ws-j01/../../../../../<repo path>' and '<...>/ws-j01/data' are accepted by both. A path outside any workspace is refused by both. Runbook l.43 says every command runs from the repository root, and mkws.sh does cd $REPO before the copy, so a relative path puts the copy inside the repository. No file in tests/ mentions mkws. Ran the proposed guard match-only too: it refuses all of these and accepts real workspace paths, with or without a trailing slash.

findings.summary: mkws.sh copies the files as they are on disk, uncommitted edits included. The runbook checks each workspace against the commit it was made from. So a copy made while the repository has uncommitted edits carries them, and the check then blames them on the agent.
findings.evidence: mkws.sh line 10: git ls-files -z | xargs -0 -I{} cp --parents {} "$WS"/ copies files from disk, not from HEAD. Runbook, "How a batch runs", step 2, checks each workspace "against the commit it was made from (<start>, in the state file)" with git show "$1:$2" | cmp -s - "$3/$2". Section 3 says "Note in the state file the commit the copies were made from". Step 1 expects the orchestrator to have uncommitted changes of its own while workflows run. I ran both runbook commands on a fresh copy and they printed nothing. After I edited README.md in the copy they printed README.md, and an orchestrator edit present at copy time would show up the same way.
findings.fix: In mkws.sh, before the copy: git diff --quiet HEAD -- || { echo "mkws.sh: the repository has uncommitted changes to tracked files; commit them first" >&2; exit 2; }. At the end, print git rev-parse HEAD next to "$WS", so the state file records the commit that was actually copied.

verdict.reason: Confirmed (minor). mkws.sh copies the files as they are on disk. Any uncommitted edit to a tracked file at copy time lands in the workspace, and the runbook's workspace check against the recorded commit then lists it as if the agent had changed it. The proposed refusal only helps if it runs before rm -rf. Otherwise a refused re-make has already deleted the job's workspace and its notes. Copying the commit itself avoids the refusal altogether.
verdict.evidence: mkws.sh l.10 copies with git ls-files and cp --parents from disk. Test: in a depth-1 clone of the repository with one uncommitted edit to README.md, a copy of mkws.sh pointed at the clone made a workspace. The runbook's changed-files command (l.94-96), run against the clone's HEAD, printed README.md; the new-files command printed nothing. Separately, git archive HEAD | tar -x into an empty folder gave exactly the 220 tracked files, none different from HEAD (.gitattributes has no export-ignore).
verdict.better_fix: Replace line 10 with: git -C "$REPO" archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$WS". End with: echo "$WS $(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse HEAD)", so the state file records the commit that was actually copied. If you keep the refusal instead, put git -C "$REPO" diff --quiet HEAD -- || { echo ... >&2; exit 2; } right after the path guard, before rm -rf.
